newsitem.title: USA: Clinton tells Democrats wants budget deal soon.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tells Democrats wants budget deal soon.

text.p: President Clinton told House Democrats Wednesday he would like a balanced budget agreement sooner rather than later to provide a boost for the economy and ward off interest rate increases, the senior Democrat on the House Budget Committee said on Wednesday.

Rep. John Spratt of South Carolina, who was among House Democrats meeting with Clinton at the White House, told reporters that the president reiterated that any budget deal reached with Republicans must have the support of a majority of Democrats to win his endorsement.

Spratt, who has participated in closed door-talks with the White House and Republicans, said he doubted any budget deal would be reached next week. "There is a wide, wide gap between us right now, and significant knotty issues," he said.

He said the next round of talks might produce an agreement simply to continue negotiations. The issue of taxes, one of the most difficult problems in the budget to work out, had not been discussed in any great detail as yet, he added.
